scoring.applicability: Raise when multiple behaviors, implementations, or interface translations create a real substitution boundary.
scoring.suitability: Raise when the abstraction removes repeated conditionals or dependency knowledge from callers.
scoring.conformance: Raise when contracts, implementations, construction, and delegation match the pattern roles.
scoring.opportunity: Raise when a proven variation axis exists, current conformance is low, and the abstraction would remove more machinery than it adds.

migration_cautions: Introduce object abstractions only around multiple real implementations or a demonstrated substitution boundary.

cards.name: Abstract Factory
cards.intent: Create compatible families of related objects without coupling clients to concrete classes.
semantic_questions: Must clients switch an entire compatible product family together?
benefits: Centralizes family selection and prevents incompatible product combinations.
liabilities: Adding a new product role can require changing every factory implementation.
verification_invariants: Each factory yields a mutually compatible product family.

cards.name: Adapter
cards.intent: Translate an existing interface into the contract expected by a client.
semantic_questions: Is this boundary translating contracts rather than adding new business policy?
benefits: Contains external or legacy interface differences.
liabilities: Can become a dumping ground for unrelated policy and validation.
verification_invariants: Every adapted operation preserves source semantics and target contract expectations.

cards.name: Bridge
cards.intent: Separate an abstraction from an independently varying implementation hierarchy.
semantic_questions: Do abstraction and implementation represent two genuinely independent dimensions of change?
liabilities: Adds indirection when only one dimension actually varies.
verification_invariants: Every supported abstraction remains compatible with every permitted implementation.

cards.name: Composite
cards.intent: Treat individual objects and recursive groups through one common interface.
semantic_questions: Can clients apply the same meaningful operation to leaves and containers?
benefits: Makes recursive structures uniform for callers.
liabilities: A broad common interface can force meaningless operations onto leaves.
verification_invariants: Container behavior is the defined composition of child behavior.

cards.name: Decorator
cards.intent: Add composable behavior around an object while retaining its contract.
semantic_questions: Is the added responsibility independently optional and order-aware?
benefits: Supports runtime composition without subclass explosion.
liabilities: Many wrappers can obscure execution order and identity.
verification_invariants: The wrapped object remains substitutable and decoration order is tested.

cards.name: Dependency Inversion
cards.intent: Make high-level policy depend on stable abstractions rather than volatile implementation details.
semantic_questions: Is there a volatile dependency with multiple implementations or a boundary worth isolating?
benefits: Stabilizes policy code across infrastructure changes.
liabilities: Speculative interfaces increase navigation and configuration cost.
verification_invariants: High-level behavior is testable against the abstraction and no implementation detail leaks through.

cards.name: Facade
cards.intent: Offer a focused entry point over a more complex subsystem.
semantic_questions: Can the subsystem's common use cases be expressed through one cohesive boundary?
benefits: Reduces client coupling and reveals supported workflows.
liabilities: A facade can grow into an oversized service that owns unrelated behavior.
verification_invariants: Facade operations preserve subsystem contracts and do not conceal required advanced access.

cards.name: Factory Method
cards.intent: Delegate construction choice while keeping the creation protocol stable.
semantic_questions: Does construction vary independently from the operation that uses the object?
liabilities: Subclass-based creation can be heavier than passing a callable.
verification_invariants: Every factory result satisfies the declared product contract.

cards.name: God Object
cards.intent: Identify a type that centralizes many unrelated responsibilities and collaborators.
semantic_questions: Which responsibilities change for different reasons or serve different callers?
benefits: Surfaces concentrated change risk and low cohesion.
liabilities: Mechanical splitting can create chatty objects and broken invariants.
verification_invariants: Any split retains ownership of cross-responsibility invariants and transaction boundaries.

cards.name: Inappropriate Inheritance
cards.intent: Detect subtype relationships used for reuse despite weak substitutability.
semantic_questions: Can every subtype honor the base contract without disabling or redefining operations?
benefits: Exposes fragile reuse and violated substitutability.
liabilities: Replacing inheritance can lose framework-required extension semantics.
verification_invariants: Every replacement preserves polymorphic behavior expected by current clients.

cards.name: Leaky Abstraction
cards.intent: Identify an abstraction that forces callers to understand hidden implementation details.
semantic_questions: Can callers use the abstraction correctly without knowing the selected implementation?
benefits: Reveals boundaries that fail to contain volatility.
liabilities: Some operational characteristics cannot or should not be hidden.
verification_invariants: The repaired contract exposes necessary capabilities without implementation-specific coupling.

cards.name: Provider Abstraction
cards.intent: Define one stable provider contract for multiple interchangeable external or model implementations.
semantic_questions: Do at least two real providers share stable semantics, lifecycle, and error expectations?
benefits: Removes provider conditionals from clients and supports runtime substitution.
liabilities: A lowest-common-denominator interface can hide provider-specific capabilities.
verification_invariants: Every provider passes the same contract suite and records provider-specific provenance separately.

cards.name: Proxy
cards.intent: Control access to another object while preserving its client-facing contract.
semantic_questions: Is the added behavior access control, location, caching, or lifecycle rather than domain policy?
benefits: Encapsulates access concerns behind a substitutable boundary.
liabilities: Remote or lazy behavior can make cost and failure less visible.
verification_invariants: Proxy-visible behavior matches the subject contract including error semantics.

cards.name: State
cards.intent: Delegate behavior to explicit state objects when valid operations vary by lifecycle state.
semantic_questions: Are states stable domain concepts with distinct behavior and transition rules?
liabilities: Creates many types for a small or mostly data-driven lifecycle.
verification_invariants: Only declared transitions occur and every state preserves shared invariants.

cards.name: Strategy
cards.intent: Encapsulate interchangeable algorithms behind one stable operation contract.
semantic_questions: Do multiple real algorithms solve the same problem under the same preconditions?
benefits: Makes algorithm selection explicit and removes caller conditionals.
liabilities: Adds object and configuration overhead for trivial variation.
verification_invariants: All strategies satisfy shared inputs, outputs, errors, and domain invariants.

cards.name: Template Method
cards.intent: Fix an algorithm skeleton while allowing selected steps to vary through overrides.
semantic_questions: Is the invariant sequence more stable than the individual customizable steps?
benefits: Keeps workflow order centralized while exposing narrow extension points.
liabilities: Inheritance couples extensions to lifecycle and protected implementation details.
verification_invariants: Overrides cannot bypass mandatory steps or shared cleanup.
